import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date column to datetime
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Create a bar chart to show the average sales by product
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x='product', y='total', data=coffee_sales)
plt.title('Average Sales by Product')
plt.xlabel('Product')
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot to show the relationship between quantity and price
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.scatterplot(x='quantity', y='price', data=coffee_sales)
plt.title('Relationship between Quantity and Price')
plt.xlabel('Quantity')
plt.ylabel('Price ($)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_scatter.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a histogram to show the distribution of customer age groups
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.histplot(x='customer_age_group', data=coffee_sales, kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Customer Age Groups')
plt.xlabel('Customer Age Group')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_age_group.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a pie chart to show the payment method distribution
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))
sns.countplot(x='payment_method', data=coffee_sales)
plt.title('Payment Method Distribution')
plt.xlabel('Payment Method')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_payment.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
